page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn5-c28g1.7xlarge is a GPU-accelerated server instance belonging to the ecs.gn5 family. It is equipped with 28 dedicated Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 physical cores operating at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 112 GB of system memory, providing 4 GB of RAM per core. For acceleration, the instance features a single NVIDIA P100 GPU based on the Pascal architecture with 16 GB of VRAM. Local storage consists of a 472 GB SSD, and the baseline network bandwidth is rated at 5 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates a clear contrast between CPU and GPU capabilities. Single-core CPU performance is in the bottom 10% according to stress-ng, and single-threaded compression tasks are weak, falling into the bottom 25%. However, multi-core CPU performance, memory bandwidth, and static web serving throughput register in the middle 50%. The hardware excels in specific machine learning tasks, with LLM inference speed for prompt processing on both 135M and 7B models reaching the top 10%, and text generation on the 7B model also scoring in the top tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance leverages an older generation NVIDIA Pascal GPU and Intel Broadwell CPU architecture. This hardware profile offers a balanced resource density of compute, memory, and local SSD storage, making it a qualitatively cost-effective option for legacy GPU workloads that do not require modern tensor cores. The primary tradeoff is the weak single-core CPU execution speed, meaning workloads must be highly parallelized or GPU-bound to justify the resource allocation.

This instance is designed for workloads such as medium-scale LLM inference, parallelized scientific computing, database operations, and static web serving. The combination of dedicated cores, local SSD storage, and dedicated GPU VRAM supports workloads that benefit from GPU acceleration without requiring the highest single-thread CPU performance.
